claims: CO2 methanation can store renewable hydrogen in the gas grid.
Ni-based catalysts are active at low temperature but can produce CO.
Defect engineering has been proposed to tune CH4 selectivity, yet comparisons rarely fix the space velocity.

works.summary: Defect sites raised low-temperature activity of Ni catalysts.
works.limitation: Space velocity was not fixed, so the defect effect is mixed with contact-time effects.

works.summary: Bimetallic NiCo catalysts changed product distribution at low temperature.
works.limitation: Only conversion was reported; CH4 selectivity was not compared under identical conditions.

related_work_groups.synthesis: Both routes report activity gains, but neither isolates the defect effect on selectivity at a fixed space velocity.

works.summary: Reviewed selectivity metrics and showed that conversion-normalised and raw selectivities can rank catalysts differently.
works.limitation: The review did not test low-temperature NiCo catalysts.

works.summary: Reported conversion without a selectivity metric.
works.limitation: The missing selectivity metric prevents comparison with selectivity-focused studies.

related_work_groups.synthesis: Metric choice is inconsistent across studies, so cross-paper selectivity claims are not directly comparable.

gap.statement: Defect engineering is proposed to improve CH4 selectivity, but existing studies either vary space velocity or omit selectivity metrics; a same-condition comparison of defect-rich and defect-poor NiCo catalysts is therefore missing.
evidence: synthetic-manuscript.md P006: comparisons rarely fix the space velocity
chen2019 limitation: space velocity not fixed

contributions.statement: We compare NiCo-200 and NiCo-50 at a fixed space velocity and show 85% versus 65% CH4 selectivity at 250 °C.
We bound the operating window by showing that NiCo-200 selectivity decreases above 275 °C.
We identify the unmeasured defect concentration as the remaining mechanistic uncertainty.
evidence: synthetic-manuscript.md P013: defect concentration was not measured operando

citation_coverage.claim: Defect sites were reported to raise low-temperature activity, without a fixed space velocity.
Bimetallic catalysts changed product distribution but selectivity metrics were incomplete.
Selectivity metrics are inconsistent across CO2 hydrogenation studies.
